events.title: Farming in the Zagros
events.description: At Chogha Golan in the foothills of the Zagros people cultivate wild barley for two thousand years until it becomes a domesticated crop.

events.title: Goats are domesticated at Ganj Dareh
events.description: Bones from a village in the Zagros show herders managing goats, among the earliest evidence anywhere.

events.title: Susa is founded
events.description: A settlement on the Khuzestan plain becomes one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

events.title: Proto-Elamite writing
events.description: Clay tablets at Susa carry one of the world's earliest writing systems. Most of it is still undeciphered.

events.title: Shahr-e Sukhteh, the Burnt City
events.description: A Bronze Age city in the eastern desert leaves an artificial eyeball, an early backgammon set and a goblet that may be the first animation.

events.title: Jiroft and the Halil River
events.description: Carved chlorite vessels from Kerman reveal a culture nobody knew existed until floods and looters exposed its cemeteries in 2001.

events.title: The ziggurat of Chogha Zanbil
events.description: The Elamite king Untash-Napirisha builds a stepped temple complex near Susa, still among the best preserved ziggurats.

events.title: Zarathustra
events.description: A priest-poet whose dates are still argued over by centuries teaches a contest between truth and the lie. Zoroastrianism becomes the faith of three Persian empires.

events.title: The Medes and the Persians arrive
events.description: Iranian-speaking peoples settle the plateau. Assyrian records first name the Parsua and the Madai.

events.title: Assyria destroys Susa
events.description: Ashurbanipal sacks the Elamite capital, salts the land and boasts of it. Elam never recovers.

events.title: The Medes help take Nineveh
events.description: A Median and Babylonian alliance destroys the Assyrian capital. The Median kingdom at Ecbatana becomes the first Iranian empire.

events.title: Cyrus founds the Persian Empire
events.description: Cyrus of Anshan overthrows his Median overlord and within twenty years rules from the Aegean to Central Asia.

events.title: Cyrus takes Babylon
events.description: Babylon falls almost without a fight. The Cyrus Cylinder records the restoration of temples, and the Bible records the Jews' return from exile.

events.title: Cambyses conquers Egypt
events.description: Cyrus's son adds Egypt, and the empire is the largest the world has yet seen.

events.title: The Behistun inscription
events.description: Darius carves his account of seizing the throne on a cliff in three languages. Copied by Henry Rawlinson in the 1830s, it unlocks cuneiform.

events.title: Persepolis is begun
events.description: Darius starts a ceremonial capital whose reliefs show delegations from every corner of the empire bringing tribute.

events.title: Satrapies and the Royal Road
events.description: Darius organises the empire into provinces with fixed tribute, a common coinage and a road from Susa to Sardis that couriers cover in a week.

events.title: Marathon
events.description: A Persian landing in Attica is beaten by the Athenians. For Persia it is a frontier setback; for the Greeks it becomes a founding myth.

events.title: Xerxes invades Greece
events.description: Xerxes crosses the Hellespont, wins at Thermopylae and burns Athens, then loses his fleet at Salamis.

events.title: Gaugamela
events.description: Alexander defeats Darius III. Darius is murdered by his own satrap the next year and the Achaemenid line ends.

events.title: Alexander burns Persepolis
events.description: The palace is set alight after a drinking party, in revenge for Athens or by accident. Zoroastrian tradition remembers him as the accursed.

events.title: The Seleucid kingdom
events.description: One of Alexander's generals takes the eastern empire. Greek cities are founded across Iran.

events.title: The Parthians rise
events.description: Arsaces leads the Parni into the province of Parthia, and his dynasty rules Iran for nearly five centuries.

events.title: Mithridates I takes Mesopotamia
events.description: The Parthians reach the Tigris and build their winter capital at Ctesiphon.

events.title: The Silk Road opens through Iran
events.description: Envoys from Han China reach the Parthian court. Iran sits astride the trade between Rome and China for centuries.

events.title: Carrhae
events.description: Parthian horse archers destroy the army of Crassus. Seven legions are lost and their eagles taken.

events.title: The Avesta takes shape
events.description: Tradition holds that the Parthian court begins collecting the scattered Zoroastrian scriptures, a work the Sasanians finish.

events.title: Trajan takes Ctesiphon
events.description: The Roman emperor reaches the Persian Gulf. His successor gives it all back.

events.title: Ardashir founds the Sasanian Empire
events.description: A Persian vassal defeats the last Parthian king and founds a dynasty that calls its realm Eranshahr, the land of the Iranians.

events.title: Shapur captures a Roman emperor
events.description: Valerian is taken at Edessa. Shapur carves the scene of Roman emperors kneeling before him at Naqsh-e Rustam.

events.title: Mani is executed
events.description: The prophet of a religion blending Zoroastrian, Christian and Buddhist ideas dies in prison. Manichaeism spreads from Rome to China.

events.title: Jundishapur
events.description: A Sasanian city in Khuzestan grows into a centre of medicine, later hosting Greek, Syriac and Indian scholars.

events.title: The Mazdakite movement
events.description: A preacher teaches common ownership of property, and King Kavad backs him for a time before Mazdak and his followers are massacred.

events.title: Khosrow I, the Just
events.description: Khosrow reforms taxation and the army and welcomes Greek philosophers expelled by Justinian. Chess arrives from India in his reign.

events.title: The last great war with Rome
events.description: Twenty-six years of war take Persian armies to Jerusalem, Egypt and the walls of Constantinople, then back again. Both empires are left exhausted.

events.title: Defeat at Qadisiyyah
events.description: An Arab Muslim army defeats the Sasanian field army in Iraq. Ctesiphon falls the next year.

events.title: Nahavand
events.description: The last imperial army is destroyed in the Zagros. The Arabs call it the victory of victories.

events.title: Yazdegerd III is killed at Merv
events.description: The last Sasanian king, a fugitive in his own empire, is murdered by a miller. His son flees to China.

events.title: Zoroastrians leave for India
events.description: Groups of Zoroastrians emigrate to Gujarat over the following centuries. Their descendants are the Parsis.

events.title: The Abbasid revolution starts in Khorasan
events.description: A revolt raised in eastern Iran under Abu Muslim overthrows the Umayyads. Persian administrators run the new caliphate from Baghdad.

events.title: Al-Khwarizmi
events.description: A scholar from Khwarazm writes on solving equations. His book gives us algebra, and his name gives us algorithm.

events.title: The Samanids
events.description: An Iranian dynasty rules from Bukhara and patronises poetry in New Persian, written in Arabic script. Persian becomes a literary language again.

events.title: The Buyids take Baghdad
events.description: A Daylamite family from the Caspian controls the caliph. For a century the Abbasids reign while Iranians rule.

events.title: Ferdowsi finishes the Shahnameh
events.description: After thirty years the poet completes fifty thousand couplets of Iran's kings and heroes, written almost without Arabic words. It is still recited in teahouses.

events.title: Avicenna's Canon of Medicine
events.description: Ibn Sina completes the medical encyclopedia that Europe's universities teach from for six hundred years.

events.title: The Seljuks win at Dandanaqan
events.description: Turkic nomads defeat the Ghaznavids and take Iran. Within twenty years they rule Baghdad as sultans.

events.title: Nizam al-Mulk and the Nizamiyya
events.description: The Persian vizier of the Seljuks founds colleges across the empire, and the madrasa becomes the model Islamic school.

events.title: Hassan-i Sabbah takes Alamut
events.description: An Ismaili leader seizes a mountain fortress and runs a network of strongholds and targeted killings. Europe calls his followers the Assassins.

events.title: Omar Khayyam and the calendar
events.description: The mathematician leads a team that reforms the solar calendar, more accurately than the Gregorian. His quatrains become famous in English eight centuries later.

events.title: The Mongols arrive
events.description: Genghis Khan's armies destroy the cities of Khorasan. Merv, Nishapur and Herat are massacred and the population of the east falls for generations.

events.title: Hulagu takes Alamut
events.description: Genghis's grandson destroys the Assassin castles and founds the Ilkhanate, then sacks Baghdad in 1258.

events.title: Saadi's Gulistan
events.description: The Shirazi poet finishes the Rose Garden. A line of it about humanity as one body hangs at the United Nations.

events.title: The observatory at Maragheh
events.description: Nasir al-Din Tusi builds an observatory for Hulagu. His models of planetary motion turn up later in Copernicus.

events.title: Ghazan converts to Islam
events.description: The Ilkhan becomes a Muslim, and his vizier Rashid al-Din writes a history of the whole known world.

events.title: Hafez
events.description: The poet of Shiraz writes the ghazals still used for divination in Iranian homes. A copy of his Divan sits in most of them.

events.title: Timur's campaigns
events.description: Timur sweeps through Iran, building towers of skulls at Isfahan. Under his successors Herat becomes a centre of Persian painting.

events.title: Ismail founds the Safavid state
events.description: A fourteen-year-old Sufi leader takes Tabriz and proclaims Twelver Shiism the state religion. Most Iranians are Sunni at the time.

events.title: Chaldiran
events.description: Ottoman cannon defeat Ismail's cavalry. The border settles roughly where Iran meets Turkey today.

events.title: The peace of Amasya
events.description: The first formal treaty with the Ottomans divides the Caucasus and Mesopotamia.

events.title: Shah Abbas the Great
events.description: Abbas builds a standing army of slave soldiers, curbs the tribal chiefs and wins back the lands lost to the Ottomans and Uzbeks.

events.title: Isfahan becomes the capital
events.description: Abbas lays out a vast square framed by mosques and the bazaar. Isfahan is half the world, says the proverb.

events.title: Hormuz is taken from Portugal
events.description: With English ships, Abbas expels the Portuguese from the island that controlled the Gulf trade.

events.title: The treaty of Zuhab
events.description: Iraq goes to the Ottomans. The line agreed is roughly today's Iran-Iraq border.

events.title: The Afghans take Isfahan
events.description: After a six-month siege in which much of the city starves, Afghan rebels end Safavid rule.

events.title: Nader Shah
events.description: A general of humble birth drives out the Afghans and Ottomans and crowns himself. Three years later he sacks Delhi and returns with the Peacock Throne.

events.title: Karim Khan Zand
events.description: A ruler who calls himself only the regent of the people governs from Shiraz in relative peace for nearly thirty years.

events.title: Agha Mohammad Khan founds the Qajars
events.description: A eunuch chieftain reunites Iran with great cruelty and makes Tehran the capital.

events.title: The treaty of Gulistan
events.description: Defeat by Russia costs Iran Georgia, Dagestan and most of Azerbaijan.

events.title: The treaty of Turkmenchay
events.description: A second war with Russia loses Armenia and Nakhchivan and grants Russians legal immunity in Iran. Iran's modern northern border is set.

events.title: The Bab
events.description: A merchant of Shiraz proclaims himself the gate to the hidden imam. He is executed in Tabriz in 1850, and the Baha'i faith grows from his movement.

events.title: Herat is given up
events.description: After a short war with Britain, Iran renounces its claim to Herat. Afghanistan takes shape as a buffer.

events.title: The tobacco protest
events.description: The shah sells a monopoly on tobacco to a British subject. A fatwa against smoking is obeyed across the country, even in the harem, and the concession is cancelled.

events.title: The Constitutional Revolution
events.description: Protesters take sanctuary in the British legation and win a constitution and the first parliament, the Majlis.

events.title: Britain and Russia divide Iran
events.description: The two powers agree spheres of influence, the Russians in the north and the British in the southeast, without asking Iran.

events.title: Oil at Masjed Soleyman
events.description: After seven years of drilling, a British syndicate strikes oil in Khuzestan. The Anglo-Persian Oil Company, later BP, follows.

events.title: The great famine
events.description: Wartime occupation, requisitioning and failed harvests kill a large share of the population. Estimates run from hundreds of thousands to several million.

events.title: Reza Khan's coup
events.description: A Cossack officer marches on Tehran with British encouragement and takes the war ministry.

events.title: Reza Shah founds the Pahlavi dynasty
events.description: The Majlis deposes the Qajars and crowns Reza Khan. He builds railways, a national army and modern schools by decree.

events.title: Persia becomes Iran
events.description: Reza Shah asks foreign governments to use the name Iranians have always used for their country.

events.title: The unveiling decree
events.description: The chador is banned in public. Police tear veils off women in the street, and many older women stop leaving home.

events.title: The Trans-Iranian Railway
events.description: A line from the Caspian to the Gulf is finished without foreign loans. It becomes the Allies' supply route to the Soviet Union.

events.title: The Anglo-Soviet invasion
events.description: Britain and the Soviet Union occupy Iran to secure the oil and the railway, and force Reza Shah to abdicate for his son Mohammad Reza.

events.title: The Tehran Conference
events.description: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet for the first time, at the Soviet embassy in Tehran.

events.title: Mossadegh nationalises oil
events.description: The Majlis takes over the British oil company. Britain blockades Iranian oil, and Mossadegh is Time's man of the year.

events.title: The coup against Mossadegh
events.description: A coup organised by the CIA and MI6 removes the elected prime minister and restores the shah's power. It shadows every American relationship with Iran since.

events.title: SAVAK
events.description: The shah's secret police is founded with American and Israeli help. It becomes notorious for torture.

events.title: The White Revolution
events.description: Land reform, votes for women and a literacy corps. A cleric named Ruhollah Khomeini attacks it and is exiled the next year.

events.title: The Persepolis celebrations
events.description: The shah throws a party in the desert for 2,500 years of monarchy, with food flown from Maxim's of Paris, while much of the country is poor.

events.title: The oil boom
events.description: Oil prices quadruple. Money floods in, inflation and shanty towns follow, and the gap between Tehran's north and south becomes the story.

events.title: Black Friday
events.description: Troops fire on demonstrators in Jaleh Square in Tehran. Strikes shut the oil fields by the end of the year.

events.title: The shah leaves
events.description: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi flies out with a box of Iranian soil. He dies in Egypt eighteen months later.

events.title: Khomeini returns
events.description: Several million people line the streets of Tehran for the ayatollah's return from fifteen years of exile.

events.title: The Islamic Republic
events.description: A referendum makes Iran an Islamic Republic, and a new constitution puts a senior cleric, the Supreme Leader, above the elected government.

events.title: The embassy hostage crisis
events.description: Students seize the American embassy and hold fifty-two hostages for 444 days. Relations with the United States have never been restored.

events.title: Iraq invades
events.description: Saddam Hussein attacks Khuzestan. Eight years of war follow, with chemical weapons, human-wave assaults and perhaps half a million Iranians dead.

events.title: The war ends, and the prison executions
events.description: Khomeini accepts a ceasefire he says is worse than drinking poison. Within weeks several thousand political prisoners are executed.

events.title: Khamenei succeeds Khomeini
events.description: Khomeini dies and Ali Khamenei, then a mid-ranking cleric, becomes Supreme Leader.

events.title: Khatami's landslide
events.description: A reformist cleric wins the presidency with 70% of the vote on promises of civil society and dialogue among civilisations.

events.title: The student protests
events.description: Security forces raid a Tehran University dormitory, and six days of protests are crushed.

events.title: The Bam earthquake
events.description: An earthquake destroys the city of Bam and its mud-brick citadel and kills over twenty-six thousand people.

events.title: The Green Movement
events.description: Millions protest Ahmadinejad's disputed re-election. The death of Neda Agha-Soltan, filmed on a phone, is seen worldwide.

events.title: Iran wins an Oscar
events.description: Asghar Farhadi's A Separation wins the Academy Award for foreign language film. He wins again in 2017 and boycotts the ceremony.

events.title: The nuclear deal
events.description: Iran agrees limits on its nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief. The United States withdraws in 2018.

events.title: Soleimani is killed
events.description: An American drone kills the commander of the Quds Force in Baghdad. Days later Iran shoots down a Ukrainian airliner by mistake.

events.title: Woman, Life, Freedom
events.description: Mahsa Amini dies in the custody of the morality police after being arrested for her headscarf. Months of protests follow, led by young women.

events.title: The twelve-day war
events.description: Israel strikes Iranian nuclear sites and commanders, the United States bombs Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, and Iran fires missiles at Israel before a ceasefire.
